lessons.title: Add signed numbers
lessons.reading: Adding a negative moves left on a number line. Opposite quantities can cancel; keep track of the direction and size.

lessons.title: Multiply signed numbers
lessons.reading: One negative factor gives a negative product; two negative factors give a positive product. First determine the sign, then multiply magnitudes.
lessons.easyReading: One negative factor gives a negative product; two negative factors give a positive product. First determine the sign, then multiply magnitudes.
lessons.expertReading: One negative factor gives a negative product; two negative factors give a positive product. First determine the sign, then multiply magnitudes. The sign rules preserve the distributive property across positive and negative values.

application.explanation: 12. One negative factor gives a negative product; two negative factors give a positive product. First determine the sign, then multiply magnitudes.

vocab.definition: A number expressible as a ratio of integers with a nonzero denominator.

lessons.title: Proportional relationships
lessons.reading: In a proportional relationship, y/x is constant for nonzero x. The equation is y = kx and its graph passes through the origin.
lessons.easyReading: In a proportional relationship, y/x is constant for nonzero x. The equation is y = kx and its graph passes through the origin.
lessons.expertReading: In a proportional relationship, y/x is constant for nonzero x. The equation is y = kx and its graph passes through the origin. A fixed starting fee produces a linear relationship that is not proportional.

lessons.title: Percent change
lessons.reading: Percent change compares the change with the original value. Divide change by original, then multiply by 100.
lessons.easyReading: Percent change compares the change with the original value. Divide change by original, then multiply by 100.
lessons.expertReading: Percent change compares the change with the original value. Divide change by original, then multiply by 100. Reversing a percent change uses a different original value, so the percentages need not match.
lessons.worked: A price rises from $40 to $50. The $10 increase is 10/40 = 25%.

application.prompt: A price drops from $80 to $60. What is the percent decrease?
application.explanation: 25%. Percent change compares the change with the original value. Divide change by original, then multiply by 100.

vocab.definition: A change expressed as a percentage of the original amount.

lessons.practice: Explain how percent change helps solve the question. Include the numbers or properties that support your answer.
lessons.reflection: 25%. Percent change compares the change with the original value. Divide change by original, then multiply by 100.

lessons.title: Chance as a fraction
lessons.reading: For equally likely outcomes, probability is favorable outcomes divided by all possible outcomes. It lies between zero and one.
lessons.easyReading: For equally likely outcomes, probability is favorable outcomes divided by all possible outcomes. It lies between zero and one.
lessons.expertReading: For equally likely outcomes, probability is favorable outcomes divided by all possible outcomes. It lies between zero and one. The complement of an event has probability one minus the event’s probability.
lessons.worked: A fair die has three even faces among six, so P(even) = 3/6 = 1/2.
steps: A fair die has three even faces among six, so P(even) = 3/6 = 1/2.
